1.description: Evergreen sword ferns standing tall through winter rain, fronds deep green and glistening wet
1.childFriendlyNote: These big green ferns never lose their leaves. Run your finger along one and feel the tiny bumps underneath

1.description: Varied thrush singing its haunting single-note whistle from deep in dripping Douglas fir forests
1.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful orange-and-black bird sings one loooong spooky note from the foggy trees, like a ghost flute!

1.description: Mosses at their most vibrant green, coating every branch, trunk, and rock in the rainy forest
1.childFriendlyNote: Everything is wearing a soft green blanket! Press your hand gently on a mossy log. It feels like a tiny spongy forest

1.description: Anna's hummingbirds visiting winter-blooming flowers and feeders, males flashing magenta gorgets
1.childFriendlyNote: A tiny jewel-bird hovers at a feeder even in winter. Its throat flashes bright pink when the light hits it!

1.description: Tiny Pacific wrens creeping through tangled roots and fallen logs, giving sharp 'chip' calls
1.childFriendlyNote: The tiniest brown bird hops through the dark tangly roots. It's so small it can disappear into a log!

2.description: Sword ferns lush and green on the forest floor, raindrops beading on their waxy fronds
2.childFriendlyNote: Hold a fern frond sideways and watch the raindrops roll off like tiny silver marbles

2.description: Varied thrush foraging on wet ground under conifers, flipping leaves for insects
2.childFriendlyNote: Listen in the rainy woods for a long, eerie whistle. That's the varied thrush, the voice of the Pacific Northwest winter

2.description: Male Anna's hummingbirds performing spectacular dive displays, climbing high then plummeting with a loud squeak
2.childFriendlyNote: Watch for a tiny bird zooming straight up into the sky, then diving down with a loud squeak. He's showing off!

2.description: Bald eagles perching in tall conifers near rivers, white heads visible from far away
2.childFriendlyNote: Look for a huge bird with a bright white head sitting in the tallest tree by the river. That's a bald eagle!

2.description: Licorice ferns growing from mossy branches of bigleaf maples, green and lush in winter rain
2.childFriendlyNote: These ferns grow right on tree branches in the moss. Their roots really do taste like licorice!

2.description: Banana slugs active on the wet forest floor, bright yellow bodies leaving silver slime trails
2.childFriendlyNote: A big bright-yellow slug slides slowly across the leaves. It looks just like a banana and leaves a shiny silver trail!

3.description: Mosses reaching peak lushness, bright emerald green on every surface in the rain-soaked forest
3.childFriendlyNote: Squeeze a mossy branch gently. Water drips out like a tiny sponge! Moss holds water like a rain-catcher

3.description: Anna's hummingbirds beginning to build nests, tiny cups of lichen and spider silk on sheltered branches
3.childFriendlyNote: The mama hummingbird is building a nest the size of a walnut from spider webs and tiny bits of lichen!

3.description: Flocks of Oregon juncos foraging under bushes, flashing white tail feathers when they fly
3.childFriendlyNote: Little dark birds hop under the bushes scratching for seeds. When they fly, white stripes flash on their tails like tiny flags!

3.description: Witch hazel blooming with spidery yellow or red flowers on bare branches, fragrant on mild days
3.childFriendlyNote: Crinkly yellow flowers bloom on bare twigs in January! Lean in close. They smell sweet like perfume in winter

3.description: Great blue herons standing motionless at pond edges and streams, hunting fish and frogs in the rain
3.childFriendlyNote: A giant grey bird stands perfectly still by the water like a statue. Then snap, it catches a fish!

4.description: Snowdrops blooming in gardens and parks, white bell-shaped flowers nodding in the rain
4.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bell-flowers push up through the cold ground. They're so brave they bloom while it's still winter!

4.description: Varied thrush still singing its haunting whistle from the misty forest canopy
4.childFriendlyNote: One long whistle echoes through the foggy trees. The varied thrush sounds like the forest is singing to you

4.description: Oregon grape flower buds swelling, clusters of bright yellow starting to open on holly-like evergreen shrubs
4.childFriendlyNote: Look for a bush with spiky leaves like holly. Yellow flower buds are getting ready to pop open!

4.description: Pacific wrens beginning to sing their incredibly long, bubbling song from root tangles and stream banks
4.childFriendlyNote: A bird smaller than your fist sings a song so long and fast you can't believe it, like a tiny music box!

4.description: Spotted towhees scratching noisily through leaf litter, kicking both feet backward to find food
4.childFriendlyNote: Scritch-scratch! A bird with fiery red eyes kicks leaves everywhere like a tiny soccer player looking for bugs

5.description: Oregon grape blooming bright yellow, clusters of small flowers attracting the first bees
5.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow flowers light up the forest edge. Lean close and smell them, they're like tiny sunbursts!

5.description: First crocuses appearing in lawns and garden beds, purple, yellow, and white chalice-shaped flowers
5.childFriendlyNote: Little purple and yellow cups poke up through the grass. Spring is sending its first tiny messengers!

5.description: Western skunk cabbage pushing bright yellow spathes through swampy ground, one of the earliest native wildflowers
5.childFriendlyNote: A glowing yellow flower pushes up from the mud in the swamp. But hold your nose, it smells like a skunk!

5.description: Anna's hummingbirds nesting, females sitting tight on walnut-sized nests of lichen and spider silk
5.childFriendlyNote: Somewhere in a sheltered bush, a hummingbird mama sits on two eggs the size of jellybeans!

5.description: Steller's jays calling loudly from conifers, bold dark blue with a tall black crest
5.childFriendlyNote: A loud blue bird with a punk-rock crest yells from the treetops. Steller's jays are the bossy birds of the forest!

6.description: Oregon grape in full bloom, bright yellow flower clusters buzzing with early bumblebees
6.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow flowers glow in the shady forest and fuzzy bumblebees are already visiting for breakfast!

6.description: Skunk cabbage yellow spathes fully open in wet areas, large bright beacons in boggy woodland
6.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow hoods glow in the swamp like lanterns. The plant makes its own heat to melt through frozen ground!

6.description: Crocuses spreading across lawns and parks, opening wide on any sunny afternoon
6.childFriendlyNote: The grass is dotted with colourful cups: crocuses only open when the sun comes out, like tiny sun-worshippers!

6.description: Male red-winged blackbirds returning to wetlands, flashing bright red shoulder patches and singing 'conk-la-ree'
6.childFriendlyNote: A shiny black bird puffs up his bright red shoulder patches and sings 'conk-la-reee!' from the cattails. He's calling dibs on his spot!

6.description: Early daffodils beginning to bloom in gardens and parks, yellow trumpets nodding in February rain
6.childFriendlyNote: Sunny yellow trumpets pop up even in the rain. Daffodils are shouting 'spring is coming soon!'

7.description: Skunk cabbage at peak bloom, yellow spathes lighting up swamps and wet forest edges
7.childFriendlyNote: The swamp is full of glowing yellow flowers! They make their own heat. Hold your hand near one and feel the warmth

7.description: First red-flowering currant buds swelling, clusters of pink-red flowers about to open on bare branches
7.childFriendlyNote: Pink buds are getting fat on the currant bushes. Soon they'll dangle like tiny bunches of pink grapes!

7.description: Daffodils in full bloom across gardens and parks, bright yellow patches visible from the road
7.childFriendlyNote: Whole fields of sunny yellow trumpets! Bend down and take a sniff. Daffodils smell fresh and sweet

7.description: Red-winged blackbirds establishing territories in marshes, loud chorus of 'conk-la-ree' calls at dawn
7.childFriendlyNote: Walk near a pond and you'll hear dozens of birds singing 'conk-la-reee!' The blackbirds are back!

7.description: Pacific wrens singing their spectacular bubbling song, a cascade of notes lasting up to 10 seconds
7.childFriendlyNote: Close your eyes by a stream and listen. A tiny brown bird sings a song so long and fast it sounds like a waterfall of music!

8.description: Red-flowering currant beginning to bloom, drooping clusters of rosy-pink flowers on bare branches
8.childFriendlyNote: Droopy bunches of pink flowers hang from bare branches. Lean in and smell, they have a spicy, musky scent!

8.description: Crocuses at peak bloom in lawns, parks, and playing fields, carpets of purple, white, and gold
8.childFriendlyNote: The grass has turned into a paint palette: purple, yellow, and white flowers everywhere you look!

8.description: Pacific tree frogs beginning their chorus at dusk in ponds and wetlands, a loud 'creek-it, creek-it' call
8.childFriendlyNote: Stand by a pond at sunset and listen. Tiny frogs the size of your thumb yell 'creek-it, creek-it!' so loudly!

8.description: Indian plum among the first native shrubs to leaf out, dangling clusters of small white flowers with almond scent
8.childFriendlyNote: This bush has fresh green leaves before anything else. Its white flowers smell like almonds and cucumber!

8.description: Great blue herons returning to nesting colonies in tall trees, noisy rookeries with stick nests
8.childFriendlyNote: Huge grey birds are gathering in the treetops to build nests together. They squawk and croak like dinosaurs!

9.description: Red-flowering currant in full bloom, drooping clusters of deep pink flowers mobbed by hummingbirds
9.childFriendlyNote: Pink flower bunches drip from every branch and hummingbirds zoom in to sip. It's like a hummingbird restaurant!

9.description: Pacific tree frog chorus intensifying, males calling loudly from ponds and ditches at dusk
9.childFriendlyNote: The frog chorus is getting louder! Hundreds of tiny frogs puff up their throats like bubblegum and sing 'creek-it!'

9.description: Early cherry varieties beginning to bloom in parks and streets, first clouds of pale pink flowers
9.childFriendlyNote: Pink popcorn is popping on the trees! The first cherry blossoms are opening. Spring is really here!

9.description: Salmonberry bushes showing first pink flowers on green stems along streams and forest edges
9.childFriendlyNote: Pretty pink flowers bloom on thorny green stems by the creek. Later these will turn into juicy orange berries!

9.description: Daffodils at peak bloom, masses of yellow flowers in parks, roadsides, and gardens
9.childFriendlyNote: Everywhere you look: yellow! Daffodils are blooming so thickly the ground looks like sunshine spilled on it

9.description: First rufous hummingbirds arriving from Mexico, males fiery orange-red with iridescent throat
9.childFriendlyNote: A new hummingbird arrives from far away Mexico. This one glows orange like a tiny flying ember!

10.description: Cherry blossoms opening across Portland and Seattle, pale pink clouds along streets and in parks
10.childFriendlyNote: The cherry trees are turning into pink cotton candy! Walk underneath and petals drift down like warm snow

10.description: Pacific tree frog chorus at full volume every evening, deafening near ponds and wetlands
10.childFriendlyNote: Stand by a pond at dusk and the frog chorus is so loud you have to shout, hundreds of tiny frogs singing together!

10.description: Red-flowering currant at peak, every bush dripping with pink flower clusters visited by hummingbirds
10.childFriendlyNote: Every currant bush is decorated with droopy pink flowers. Watch for hummingbirds zipping between them!

10.description: Salmonberry in bloom along streams and trails, bright pink five-petaled flowers
10.childFriendlyNote: Bright pink flowers with golden centres bloom along the creek. Bumblebees love them!

10.description: First trillium leaves unfurling on the forest floor, three-part leaf whorls with white buds just forming
10.childFriendlyNote: Three leaves in a perfect triangle are pushing up from the forest floor. A magical white flower is about to open!

10.description: Rufous hummingbirds arriving in numbers, fiery males chasing Anna's hummingbirds from feeders
10.childFriendlyNote: The feisty orange hummingbird has arrived from Mexico! It chases every other bird away from the flowers, so bossy!

11.description: Cherry blossoms opening across the region, Portland's waterfront a famous display of pink and white
11.childFriendlyNote: Whole streets are tunnels of pink! Stand under a cherry tree when the wind blows and petals swirl around you like a snow globe

11.description: Trillium beginning to bloom on the forest floor, pure white three-petaled flowers above whorls of three leaves
11.childFriendlyNote: Three white petals, three green leaves. Everything about this magical forest flower comes in threes!

11.description: Tree frog chorus still booming from every pond and wet ditch, egg masses visible in shallow water
11.childFriendlyNote: Look in the pond for blobs of jelly. Those are frog eggs! Each tiny black dot will become a tadpole

11.description: Rufous hummingbirds now common in gardens, males doing looping display flights to impress females
11.childFriendlyNote: The orange hummingbird flies in big loops in the sky to show off. He's trying to impress a lady hummingbird!

11.description: Bigleaf maple flower clusters dangling from branches before leaves emerge, greenish-yellow and fragrant
11.childFriendlyNote: Dangling green-yellow flowers hang from the bare maple branches. They smell sweet and bees go crazy for them!

12.description: Cherry blossom at peak across Portland and Seattle, streets and parks awash in pink and white petals
12.childFriendlyNote: The cherry trees are at their most magical. Pink petals carpet the ground and float through the air like confetti!

12.description: Pacific tree frogs calling loudly at dusk from every pond and wetland, the signature sound of PNW spring
12.childFriendlyNote: Creek-it, creek-it! The tiny frogs are singing their hearts out. They're only as big as your thumb but louder than a dog!

12.description: Trillium blooming across the forest floor, pure white flowers that will slowly turn pink as they age
12.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is dotted with white stars! Each trillium has exactly three petals and three leaves, nature's favourite number

12.description: Salmonberry flowers fading as tiny green berries begin forming, leaves fully unfurled along streams
12.childFriendlyNote: The pink flowers are dropping their petals and tiny green bumpy berries are growing. Soon they'll turn orange and be yummy!

12.description: Rufous hummingbirds everywhere, fiery orange males battling at feeders and flower patches
12.childFriendlyNote: The orange hummingbirds are everywhere now! Watch two zoom at each other like tiny jet fighters, so feisty!

12.description: Stream violets blooming along creeks and in damp woodland, small bright yellow flowers with purple veins
12.childFriendlyNote: Tiny yellow flowers with purple stripes hide along the creek. They're like little faces peeking up at you!

13.description: Late cherry varieties still blooming, petals beginning to fall like pink rain on windy days
13.childFriendlyNote: Pink petals swirl in the wind like a fairy snowstorm. Catch one in your hand before it touches the ground!

13.description: Trillium at peak bloom in forests, older flowers turning from white to soft pink
13.childFriendlyNote: Some trillium flowers are still white and some have blushed pink. The older they get, the more pink they turn!

13.description: First barn swallows arriving from Central America, swooping low over fields and water catching insects
13.childFriendlyNote: Sleek blue birds with forked tails zoom over the field like tiny aeroplanes. They flew all the way from Central America!

13.description: Pacific bleeding heart emerging in shady forests, fern-like leaves with dangling pink heart-shaped flowers
13.childFriendlyNote: Tiny pink hearts dangle from a delicate stem in the shade. They really do look like little valentine hearts!

13.description: Bigleaf maple flowers at peak, drooping yellow-green clusters attracting masses of bees before leaves unfurl
13.childFriendlyNote: Stand under a maple tree and hear it buzz. Hundreds of bees are visiting the dangling yellow flowers!

13.description: Rough-skinned newts migrating to ponds for breeding, brown above with vivid orange bellies
13.childFriendlyNote: A brown lizard-like creature walks slowly across the trail. Flip it gently and its belly is bright orange! (Don't touch with bare hands though)

14.description: Trillium still blooming, many flowers now turning from white to deep rose-pink with age
14.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is full of flowers changing colour. White ones are new, pink ones are old. Nature's mood ring!

14.description: Barn swallows now swooping over fields and ponds, iridescent blue backs flashing in the sun
14.childFriendlyNote: Swallows dip and dive catching bugs on the wing. They never miss! Their backs flash shiny blue like a jewel

14.description: Camas lily beginning to bloom in wet prairies, blue-violet star-shaped flowers on tall stems
14.childFriendlyNote: Blue-purple stars rise up from the wet meadow. Native people used to harvest camas bulbs for food!

14.description: Rufous hummingbirds at peak, visiting every red and orange flower in gardens and forests
14.childFriendlyNote: The fiery orange hummingbird hovers at flowers, its wings beating 50 times per second, so fast you just see a blur!

14.description: Band-tailed pigeons returning to forests, large grey pigeons with a white crescent on the nape
14.childFriendlyNote: A big grey pigeon with a white stripe on its neck coos softly from the treetops. These wild pigeons live in the forest!

15.description: Camas meadows turning blue-violet as thousands of flowers open, a stunning native prairie display
15.childFriendlyNote: The whole meadow has turned into a blue-purple ocean of flowers. It looks like the sky fell onto the grass!

15.description: Bleeding heart at peak in shady forests, clusters of dangling pink heart-shaped flowers above ferny foliage
15.childFriendlyNote: A whole row of tiny pink hearts swings gently under a fern. The forest is full of valentines!

15.description: Bigleaf maples unfurling enormous new leaves, bright lime-green against the dark conifers
15.childFriendlyNote: Huge new leaves unfold like green hands opening. Bigleaf maple leaves can grow bigger than your face!

15.description: Orange-crowned warblers singing their buzzy trill from shrubs and low trees, one of the first returning warblers
15.childFriendlyNote: A tiny yellow-green bird sings a fast buzzy trill from the bushes. It just flew here from far away!

15.description: Rough-skinned newts gathering in ponds for breeding, slow underwater dances visible in clear water
15.childFriendlyNote: Look into a clear pond and you might see newts doing a slow, dreamy dance together underwater!

16.description: Camas at peak bloom, entire prairies washed in blue-violet, one of the great wildflower shows of the PNW
16.childFriendlyNote: Fields of purple-blue flowers stretch as far as you can see, like a paintbrush dipped in the sky and swept across the meadow!

16.description: First western tiger swallowtails appearing, large yellow butterflies with black stripes gliding along streams
16.childFriendlyNote: A huge yellow butterfly with tiger stripes floats past. It's as big as your hand!

16.description: Barn swallows beginning to build mud nests under eaves and bridges, scooping mud from puddle edges
16.childFriendlyNote: Swallows carry tiny balls of mud in their beaks to build a nest under a roof, one mud-ball at a time!

16.description: New sword fern fiddleheads uncoiling from the centre of old fronds, fuzzy brown spirals unfurling
16.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy brown spirals uncurl from the fern like a snail stretching out. Watch them slowly unfold into new green fronds!

16.description: Ospreys returning to nest platforms and tall snags along rivers, carrying sticks to rebuild nests
16.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk-like bird carries a stick to the top of a pole by the river. It's building a giant nest for its family!

17.description: Early rhododendrons beginning to bloom, large clusters of pink and purple flowers on evergreen shrubs
17.childFriendlyNote: Fat flower buds are cracking open on the big shiny-leaved bushes. Huge bunches of pink flowers are about to explode!

17.description: Tiger swallowtails increasingly common, floating along streams and visiting lilacs and other garden flowers
17.childFriendlyNote: Giant yellow-and-black butterflies float lazily around the garden. They love purple flowers like lilac!

17.description: Ospreys diving feet-first into rivers to catch fish, spectacular splashing plunges
17.childFriendlyNote: Watch the osprey hover, then splash. It dives feet-first into the water and flies away with a wriggling fish!

17.description: Foxglove rosettes sending up tall flower spikes, not yet blooming but rapidly growing in forest clearings
17.childFriendlyNote: Tall green towers are shooting up from fuzzy leaf rosettes. Soon they'll be covered in purple spotted bells!

17.description: Oregon grape flowers fading, small green berry clusters forming where the yellow flowers were
17.childFriendlyNote: The yellow flowers are gone and tiny green grapes are growing in their place. They'll turn blue later!

18.description: Rhododendrons blooming across the region, massive pink and purple flower clusters in gardens and forests
18.childFriendlyNote: Huge bunches of pink flowers as big as softballs bloom on every rhododendron bush, Washington's state flower!

18.description: Nootka rose buds swelling on thorny stems along trails and hedgerows, getting ready to open
18.childFriendlyNote: Fat pink buds sit on thorny stems. Soon they'll pop open into beautiful wild roses that smell amazing!

18.description: Salmonberries ripening to orange and salmon-red along streams and forest trails
18.childFriendlyNote: Orange berries glow along the trail like tiny lanterns. Pick a ripe one and pop it in your mouth, they're sweet and squishy!

18.description: Swainson's thrush arriving from Central America, singing its rising spiral song at dusk in forests
18.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, a hidden bird sings a magical song that spirals up and up like climbing a staircase of notes!

18.description: Himalayan blackberry beginning to bloom, white five-petaled flowers on sprawling thorny canes
18.childFriendlyNote: White flowers cover the thorny blackberry bushes. Each flower will become a juicy blackberry this summer!

19.description: Rhododendrons at peak bloom, forests and gardens ablaze with pink, purple, red, and white flower clusters
19.childFriendlyNote: Every bush is like a giant bouquet! Pink, purple, and white flower balls brighten up the whole forest

19.description: Foxglove spikes beginning to open from the bottom up, purple spotted bells along tall stems in clearings
19.childFriendlyNote: Tall purple towers of bell-shaped flowers open from the bottom up. Peek inside a bell and see the spotted pattern!

19.description: Nootka rose beginning to bloom, large single pink flowers with golden centres along trails and hedgerows
19.childFriendlyNote: Wild pink roses are opening along the trail. Lean in and breathe deep, they smell like the most wonderful perfume!

19.description: Swainson's thrush now singing every evening, the magical upward-spiralling flute song of PNW summer evenings
19.childFriendlyNote: Every evening the forest fills with a dreamy, rising flute song. It spirals up like a magic spell being cast!

19.description: Blackberry bushes covered in white and pale pink flowers, humming with bees
19.childFriendlyNote: Blackberry flowers everywhere, buzzing with happy bees. Every flower you see will be a blackberry in July!

20.description: Foxglove spikes at peak bloom, tall purple towers lining forest roads and clearings
20.childFriendlyNote: Tall purple bell-towers stand like fairy castles along the forest road. Bumblebees crawl right inside each bell!

20.description: Nootka rose at peak bloom, sweet fragrance filling hedgerows and forest edges
20.childFriendlyNote: Wild roses everywhere! Close your eyes near a rose bush and just breathe. The air smells like sweet perfume

20.description: Salmonberries ripe and ready to eat, glowing orange and red berries along every stream and trail
20.childFriendlyNote: Juicy orange berries are everywhere! Gently pull a ripe one and it pops right off, sweet, squishy, and delicious!

20.description: Tree frog chorus fading as breeding season ends, tadpoles visible in shallow ponds
20.childFriendlyNote: The frog singing is quieting down, but look in the pond. Tiny black tadpoles wiggle everywhere!

20.description: Ospreys sitting on eggs in huge stick nests, one parent always on guard while the other fishes
20.childFriendlyNote: The osprey sits patiently on its big stick nest keeping eggs warm while its partner goes fishing for dinner!

21.description: Foxglove at peak, tall spires of purple bells lining roadsides, clearings, and forest margins
21.childFriendlyNote: The purple bell-towers are at their tallest! Watch a bumblebee disappear completely inside a bell and come out dusty with pollen

21.description: Blackberry flowers still going strong, petals beginning to drop as tiny green berries form behind
21.childFriendlyNote: The white flowers are falling off and tiny green bumpy berries are growing. Blackberry season is on its way!

21.description: Common yellowthroats singing 'witchity-witchity-witch' from marsh edges and dense shrubs
21.childFriendlyNote: A bright yellow bird wearing a black mask like a tiny bandit sings 'witch-ity witch-ity witch!' from the reeds

21.description: Blue elderberry bushes covered in flat clusters of tiny creamy-white flowers, sweet scent on warm days
21.childFriendlyNote: Flat plates of tiny cream-coloured flowers smell like honey and vanilla. Elderflower is used to make special drinks!

21.description: Dragonflies beginning to patrol ponds and streams, hovering and darting over the water surface
21.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom over the pond like tiny helicopters. They can fly forward, backward, and hover in place!

22.description: Rhododendrons fading, spent brown flower clusters among the glossy green leaves
22.childFriendlyNote: The big pink flowers are turning brown and papery. Rhododendron season is almost over until next year

22.description: Foxglove still blooming, upper bells opening while lower ones drop, seed pods forming below
22.childFriendlyNote: The top bells are still blooming but the bottom ones are making seed pods. The flower is like a clock counting upward!

22.description: Swainson's thrush singing its ethereal upward-spiralling song from deep in the forest every evening
22.childFriendlyNote: The evening forest fills with a song that goes up, up, up, like someone playing a flute made of starlight!

22.description: Blue dasher dragonflies perching on reed tips by ponds, powder-blue bodies with clear wings
22.childFriendlyNote: A bright blue dragonfly lands on a reed. Its see-through wings shimmer like tiny stained glass windows!

22.description: Green blackberries forming on bushes, hard and sour, slowly beginning to swell
22.childFriendlyNote: Tiny green berries cluster on the thorny bushes. They're hard and sour now but give them a month to turn sweet and black!

23.description: Blackberries swelling and starting to turn red, still sour but getting bigger by the day
23.childFriendlyNote: The blackberries are turning red, but don't eat them yet! Red means sour. Wait until they're shiny black!

23.description: Osprey chicks hatching in big stick nests, fuzzy white heads visible from below as parents bring fish
23.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy baby ospreys poke their heads up from the big nest, chirping for fish. Mum and dad take turns feeding them!

23.description: Swainson's thrush still singing at dusk, the long evenings filled with their spiralling melody
23.childFriendlyNote: The days are so long now. Sit outside at sunset and the thrush's spinning song makes the world feel magical

23.description: Yellowthroats nesting in dense marsh vegetation, males still singing from exposed perches
23.childFriendlyNote: The masked yellow bird sings his song over and over ('witch-ity witch-ity!') from the top of a cattail

23.description: Oceanspray bushes covered in cascading clusters of tiny creamy-white flowers, like frozen waterfalls
23.childFriendlyNote: Creamy white flower clusters drip from every branch like frozen ocean waves. That's why it's called oceanspray!

24.description: Blackberries turning from red to dark purple-black on sun-exposed canes, the first ripe ones appearing
24.childFriendlyNote: Some berries are turning from red to black. The black shiny ones in the sun are starting to get sweet!

24.description: Eight-spotted skimmer dragonflies cruising over ponds, black-and-white spotted wings distinctive
24.childFriendlyNote: A dragonfly with polka-dot wings zips over the pond. Count the dark spots on its wings, there are eight!

24.description: Sword fern fronds showing rows of brown spore dots on the underside, beginning to mature
24.childFriendlyNote: Flip over a fern leaf and see rows of brown dots. Those aren't bugs, they're tiny packets of baby fern dust called spores!

24.description: Bald eagle chicks growing in nests, parents bringing fish from rivers and Puget Sound
24.childFriendlyNote: Baby eagles are getting bigger in their huge nest. They're fluffy and grey and very hungry all the time!

24.description: Thimbleberry flowers finishing, green berries starting to form on the large-leaved shrubs in forest shade
24.childFriendlyNote: The big white flowers are turning into tiny green berries that look like little raspberries wearing thimble hats!

25.description: Blackberries starting to ripen in earnest, first fully black berries on south-facing brambles
25.childFriendlyNote: The first blackberries are ripe! Gently pull a shiny black one. If it comes off easily, it's ready to eat. Yum!

25.description: Bald eagles fishing along rivers and coastlines, juveniles beginning to leave the nest
25.childFriendlyNote: Young eagles are practising flying! They look scruffy and brown. It takes them four years to get a white head

25.description: The PNW dry season settling in, day after day of warm sunshine and blue skies after nine months of rain
25.childFriendlyNote: After months and months of rain, the sky finally turns bright blue every single day, summer in the Pacific Northwest is magical!

25.description: Oregon grape berries turning from green to dusty blue-purple, clusters hanging heavy on shrubs
25.childFriendlyNote: The berries are turning blue like tiny blueberries! They're very sour though. Birds and bears like them more than people do

25.description: Green darner dragonflies patrolling ponds and meadows, large with bright green thorax and blue abdomen
25.childFriendlyNote: The biggest dragonfly around zooms past. It's green and blue and can fly 60 miles per hour. Faster than a car in town!

26.description: Blackberries ripening fast in the summer heat, dark clusters heavy on every bramble patch
26.childFriendlyNote: Blackberry season is here! The juicy black berries stain your fingers purple. Pick the ones that are darkest and softest

26.description: Thimbleberries ripening to bright red in shady forest spots, soft and delicate berries that don't keep
26.childFriendlyNote: Soft red berries that look like little hats. Pick one and pop it right in your mouth because they're too squishy to take home!

26.description: Osprey chicks growing fast, almost as big as parents, standing and flapping in the nest
26.childFriendlyNote: The baby ospreys are now as big as their parents! They stand on the nest and flap their wings, practising for their first flight

26.description: Flocks of cedar waxwings feasting on ripe berries, sleek birds with yellow-tipped tails and black masks
26.childFriendlyNote: A flock of silky brown birds with black masks and yellow tail-tips swoops into the berry bushes. They eat berries like candy!

26.description: Little brown bats emerging at dusk to hunt insects over ponds and gardens in the warm summer evenings
26.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, watch for fluttery shapes zigzagging through the sky. Bats are out catching mosquitoes for dinner!

27.description: Blackberries at peak ripeness, bushes loaded with dark sweet fruit, the taste of PNW summer
27.childFriendlyNote: This is the week for blackberries! Fill a bucket, eat twice as many as you save. Your fingers will be purple for days!

27.description: Thimbleberries at peak, bright red berries under big maple-shaped leaves in forest shade
27.childFriendlyNote: Find a trail in the shade and look under the big fuzzy leaves. Soft red berries fit right over your fingertip like a little hat!

27.description: Bald eagles soaring over rivers and coastline in warm thermals, fishing in clear summer water
27.childFriendlyNote: A bald eagle circles high above on wide wings without even flapping. It rides invisible rivers of warm air!

27.description: Dragonflies everywhere over ponds and meadows, multiple species patrolling territories and hunting insects
27.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies are the coolest hunters. They catch bugs in mid-air almost every time! Watch one zoom, grab, and crunch

27.description: Oregon grape berries fully blue-black, dusty bloom coating each berry in tight clusters
27.childFriendlyNote: Dark blue-purple berries hang in bunches. They look like tiny grapes covered in dusty powder!

28.description: Blackberries at absolute peak, every bramble loaded with sweet dark berries, staining everyone's fingers
28.childFriendlyNote: The berries are so ripe they almost fall off when you touch them. The sweetest ones are warm from the sun!

28.description: Sword fern spores mature, brown rows of sporangia releasing dust-like spores when fronds are disturbed
28.childFriendlyNote: Tap the underside of a fern leaf over dark paper and watch a cloud of golden-brown dust fall. Those are tiny spores that will grow new ferns!

28.description: Cedar waxwings moving in flocks through berry-laden trees and shrubs, high-pitched 'see-see' calls
28.childFriendlyNote: A whole flock of sleek masked birds lands in the berry tree. They pass berries to each other! How polite!

28.description: Young ospreys fledging, awkward first flights near the nest, parents still bringing fish
28.childFriendlyNote: The young ospreys are taking their first wobbly flights! They flap hard and land clumsily, just like learning to ride a bike

28.description: Bats active at dusk on warm summer evenings, swooping low over gardens and ponds catching moths
28.childFriendlyNote: As the sky turns purple, bats swoop over the garden eating hundreds of mosquitoes. They're our tiny flying pest-control heroes!

29.description: Blackberry season continuing, still plenty of ripe fruit on bushes though some patches starting to dry out
29.childFriendlyNote: Still loads of blackberries! Look in the shady spots for the juiciest ones. The ones in full sun are getting dry

29.description: Great blue herons wading in shallow water, young birds from this year now fishing alongside adults
29.childFriendlyNote: Baby herons have grown up and are learning to fish! They stand very still, then stab: lunch is caught!

29.description: Garden spiders building large orb webs in hedgerows and garden corners, webs spectacular with morning dew
29.childFriendlyNote: Look for perfect circle-webs strung between bushes. In the morning they sparkle with a thousand tiny dewdrops!

29.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring on summer thermals over fields and highways, screaming their raspy call
29.childFriendlyNote: A hawk circles slowly above the field and screams keeee-aaah! That sound you hear in every movie with an eagle? That's actually a red-tail!

29.description: Pearly everlasting blooming in dry clearings and roadsides, clusters of small white papery flowers
29.childFriendlyNote: Little white papery flowers that feel dry even when they're alive. Pick one and it stays pretty for months because it's already dried!

30.description: Late blackberries still available in shaded spots, many bushes drying out in the summer heat
30.childFriendlyNote: The blackberry bushes in the sun are drying out, but check the shady side. There are still juicy ones hiding!

30.description: Orb weaver spiders getting larger, elaborate webs everywhere in gardens and forest edges
30.childFriendlyNote: Spiders are getting bigger and their webs are everywhere. Look at how perfectly the spiral is made. Spiders are amazing engineers!

30.description: Dragonflies still abundant, hunting mosquitoes and flies over warm ponds and sunny clearings
30.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies are everywhere on hot days. They eat hundreds of mosquitoes so you don't get bitten. Thank you, dragonflies!

30.description: Bald eagles fishing along rivers and coastlines, young eagles from this year practising their skills
30.childFriendlyNote: Young bald eagles are learning to fish. They splash and miss a lot! It takes practice to catch fish with your feet

30.description: Yarrow blooming in dry meadows and roadsides, flat-topped clusters of tiny white flowers
30.childFriendlyNote: Flat white flower platforms sit on top of ferny stems. Look closely and each 'flower' is actually dozens of tiny flowers!

31.description: Last good blackberries in shady spots, most bushes now drying up with withered fruit
31.childFriendlyNote: Blackberry season is almost over. Find the last sweet ones in the shade before they're gone until next year!

31.description: Large orb weaver spiders at their biggest, fat-bodied females sitting in the centre of elaborate webs
31.childFriendlyNote: The garden spider is big now! She sits in the middle of her web like a queen on her throne, waiting for dinner to fly in

31.description: Cedar waxwings still flocking through berry bushes, soft 'see-see' calls as they move together
31.childFriendlyNote: A flock of sleek birds with tiny red dots on their wings lands in the tree and gobbles every berry in minutes!

31.description: Douglas fir cones hanging on branches, distinctive 'mouse tail' bracts visible between the scales
31.childFriendlyNote: Look at a Douglas fir cone. See the little three-pointed tongues sticking out? Legend says mice hid in the cones from a forest fire and their tails stuck out!

31.description: Common nighthawks swooping over open areas at dusk, catching insects with wide gaping mouths
31.childFriendlyNote: At sunset, watch for a bird with pointy wings swooping and diving. It has a mouth so wide it scoops up bugs like a net!

32.description: Orb weaver webs glistening with morning dew, spiders at their largest and most visible
32.childFriendlyNote: Early morning is the best time to see spider webs. Every strand sparkles with dewdrops like a diamond necklace!

32.description: Red-tailed hawks perching on power poles and fence posts, young hawks from this year learning to hunt
32.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk sits on a post and stares at the field with super-sharp eyes. It can spot a mouse from way up high!

32.description: Douglas fir cones maturing, beginning to turn brown and release winged seeds
32.childFriendlyNote: Pick up a Doug fir cone and shake it. Tiny seeds with wings flutter out and helicopter down to the ground!

32.description: Swainson's thrush singing less frequently, preparing for fall migration back to Central America
32.childFriendlyNote: The beautiful spiral song is getting rarer now. The thrush is getting ready for its long journey south. Listen while you can!

32.description: Oregon grape berries fully ripe, dark blue-purple with a dusty bloom, attracting birds
32.childFriendlyNote: The dark purple berries are ripe and the birds are feasting! The berries stain your hands blue like tiny ink bombs

33.description: Orb weaver spiders at peak size, webs everywhere catching late-summer flying insects
33.childFriendlyNote: Walk carefully in the garden. Spider webs are strung between everything! The spiders are at their biggest now

33.description: Great blue herons fishing in low summer streams, long-legged silhouettes against golden grass
33.childFriendlyNote: The heron stands in the shallow stream so still it looks like a grey statue. Patience is its superpower!

33.description: Blue elderberries ripening in flat clusters, dusty blue-purple berries drooping from branches
33.childFriendlyNote: Flat bunches of dark blue berries hang from the elder tree. Birds love them! People cook them into jam and syrup

33.description: Pearly everlasting at peak, dry papery white flowers in meadows and clearings
33.childFriendlyNote: Clusters of papery white flowers feel dry and crinkly even while growing. They last forever if you pick them!

33.description: Rufous hummingbirds beginning their southward migration, fueling up on late-summer flowers and feeders
33.childFriendlyNote: The orange hummingbirds are eating extra to get fat. They're about to fly all the way back to Mexico!

34.description: Douglas fir cones falling to the forest floor, squirrels busily collecting and caching them
34.childFriendlyNote: Cones thud to the ground and squirrels race to grab them. They're saving food for winter like tiny survivalists!

34.description: Elderberries at peak ripeness, heavy purple clusters bending branches, birds feeding constantly
34.childFriendlyNote: Dark purple berry bunches hang so heavy they bend the branches. The birds are having a feast!

34.description: Red-tailed hawks circling on late-summer thermals, young hawks fully independent now
34.childFriendlyNote: Hawks ride invisible spirals of warm air round and round. They can fly without flapping for ages!

34.description: Orb weaver females getting egg-heavy, webs catching the golden light of late summer
34.childFriendlyNote: The mama spider is getting very round. She's full of eggs! Soon she'll wrap them in a silk blanket for winter

34.description: Canada geese beginning to gather in larger flocks on playing fields and parks, early restlessness before migration
34.childFriendlyNote: Big groups of geese honk loudly on the field. They're starting to get together for their long flight south!

35.description: First bigleaf maple leaves beginning to turn yellow at the edges, earliest hint of autumn colour
35.childFriendlyNote: Look at the giant maple leaves. Some edges are turning gold! Autumn is whispering that it's coming soon

35.description: Orb weaver spiders laying egg sacs wrapped in silk, webs less maintained as the season ends
35.childFriendlyNote: The spider has made a fluffy silk ball in the corner. Inside are hundreds of tiny eggs that will hatch in spring!

35.description: Canada geese flocking on fields and ponds, noisy V-formations starting to appear overhead
35.childFriendlyNote: Honk honk! Look up and see geese flying in a big V shape. They take turns being the leader at the front!

35.description: Great blue herons fishing in low streams and along the coast as summer dries out the landscape
35.childFriendlyNote: The tall grey heron fishes in the low creek. In August, the water is so shallow you can see the fish it's watching!

35.description: Red huckleberries ripe on delicate bushes growing from old stumps in the forest, tiny tart red berries
35.childFriendlyNote: Tiny red berries on wispy branches growing right out of an old tree stump. Pop one in your mouth! They're tart and tangy!

36.description: Bigleaf maple leaves yellowing, first leaves dropping along streams and forest edges
36.childFriendlyNote: Giant golden leaves are starting to twirl down from the trees. Catch one and measure it against your face!

36.description: First chinook salmon entering rivers from the ocean, beginning their epic upstream migration to spawn
36.childFriendlyNote: Big fish are swimming up the river, against the current! Chinook salmon travel hundreds of miles to lay their eggs

36.description: First autumn rains arriving after the long dry summer, the smell of wet earth filling the air
36.childFriendlyNote: After months of sunshine, the first rain falls and the ground smells amazing. That earthy smell has a name: petrichor!

36.description: Large flocks of Canada geese flying south in V-formations, honking loudly overhead
36.childFriendlyNote: V after V of honking geese fly over. If you count them there can be hundreds in one flock!

36.description: Steller's jays caching acorns and seeds for winter, noisy and busy in the canopy
36.childFriendlyNote: The blue jays are stuffing their beaks with seeds and hiding them everywhere. They remember thousands of hiding spots!

37.description: Bigleaf maple leaves turning bright gold, enormous leaves carpeting the ground under the trees
37.childFriendlyNote: The biggest leaves you've ever seen are turning golden yellow. Pick one up and use it as an umbrella!

37.description: Chinook salmon running in rivers, large fish visible in shallow riffles, some turning dark red as they near spawning
37.childFriendlyNote: Look into the river and see big fish swimming against the water. Their bodies are turning red as they get ready to lay eggs!

37.description: Vine maples turning brilliant orange and red in the understory, glowing like fire in the green forest
37.childFriendlyNote: Small maple trees in the forest are turning orange and red like flames. The dark green forest suddenly has fire in it!

37.description: Varied thrush returning to lowland forests from mountain breeding grounds, single-note whistles returning
37.childFriendlyNote: Listen! That long, spooky whistle is back in the rainy woods. The varied thrush has come down from the mountains

37.description: First chanterelle mushrooms appearing after the autumn rains, golden funnel shapes in Douglas fir forests
37.childFriendlyNote: After the rain, golden mushrooms push up through the leaves. They smell like apricots and are shaped like tiny trumpets!

38.description: Bigleaf maples at peak colour, bright gold canopy with leaves showering down in the wind
38.childFriendlyNote: Stand under a bigleaf maple when the wind blows and golden leaves swirl around you like treasure falling from the sky!

38.description: Vine maples at peak colour, brilliant orange and crimson red in forest understory and along streams
38.childFriendlyNote: The little vine maples are on fire. Bright orange and red leaves glow in the dark forest like stained glass!

38.description: Coho salmon beginning to enter rivers, bright silver fish heading upstream alongside the darker chinook
38.childFriendlyNote: Shiny silver fish are now joining the run up the river. Coho salmon are starting their incredible journey home!

38.description: Chanterelle mushrooms emerging in greater numbers under Douglas fir and hemlock after steady rain
38.childFriendlyNote: More golden trumpet mushrooms are popping up in the forest! They hide under the leaves. Look for a flash of gold

38.description: Oregon juncos returning to lowland gardens and parks for winter, flashing white tail feathers
38.childFriendlyNote: The little grey-and-brown birds with white tail stripes are back in the garden. They spent summer in the mountains!

39.description: Vine maples still blazing orange and red, leaves beginning to fall and drift along streams
39.childFriendlyNote: Bright orange leaves float down the creek like tiny boats. Toss one in and race it against a friend's leaf!

39.description: Coho salmon running strong in rivers, silvery fish leaping over obstacles and surging through rapids
39.childFriendlyNote: Fish are leaping out of the water to get up the river! Salmon jump over rocks and logs. They never give up!

39.description: Chanterelle mushrooms at peak fruiting, golden clusters pushing up through moss and leaf litter in conifer forests
39.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is dotted with golden mushrooms! They smell fruity and sweet, like the forest is baking something yummy

39.description: Bald eagles beginning to gather near salmon streams, perching in tall trees watching for spawning fish
39.childFriendlyNote: Eagles are gathering in the trees along the river. They know the salmon are coming and they want fish for dinner!

39.description: Mushroom season accelerating with rain: shaggy manes, puffballs, and coral fungi appearing in gardens and woodlands
39.childFriendlyNote: Mushrooms are everywhere after the rain! White shaggy ones, round puffy ones, and ones that look like tiny coral reefs!

40.description: Coho salmon spawning in gravel beds, males turning dark red with hooked jaws, females digging redds
40.childFriendlyNote: The salmon have turned dark red with hooked mouths. They're digging nests in the gravel to lay their eggs. It's amazing to watch!

40.description: Chanterelles at peak season, mushroom hunters heading into the woods after every rainstorm
40.childFriendlyNote: Golden chanterelles are everywhere in the rainy forest! People love to find and cook them. They smell like peach and pepper

40.description: Bigleaf maple leaves mostly fallen, huge gold and brown leaves piled deep on trails and lawns
40.childFriendlyNote: Giant crunchy leaves are piled deep on the ground. Jump in and hear them crackle! Each leaf is as big as a dinner plate!

40.description: Varied thrush now common in lowland forests, haunting single-note whistles ringing through the autumn rain
40.childFriendlyNote: The rain is back and so is the ghost-whistle bird! One long, dreamy note rings through the dripping trees

40.description: More bald eagles gathering at salmon rivers, dozens of eagles visible at prime spawning sites
40.childFriendlyNote: Eagles are lining the river trees like ornaments. Some sit with half-eaten fish, feasting on salmon!

41.description: Chum salmon entering rivers with dramatic purple-green tiger stripes, the last major salmon run of the year
41.childFriendlyNote: Stripy purple-and-green fish are swimming up the rivers! Chum salmon look like they're wearing camouflage pyjamas

41.description: Chanterelles still fruiting strongly, joined now by hedgehog mushrooms and other autumn species
41.childFriendlyNote: So many mushrooms! Golden chanterelles and spiky hedgehog mushrooms. The forest floor is like a treasure hunt!

41.description: Bald eagles at peak numbers along salmon streams, spectacular gatherings of dozens of eagles
41.childFriendlyNote: So many eagles! Trees along the river are full of them. Some are eating fish, some are stealing fish from each other!

41.description: Mosses greening up again with the autumn rain after looking brown and dry all summer
41.childFriendlyNote: The rain is waking up the moss! After being brown and crunchy all summer, it's turning soft and green again

41.description: Oregon juncos now abundant in gardens and parks, large winter flocks foraging under feeders
41.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds with white tail flashers hop around the garden in big groups. They'll be here all winter!

42.description: Chum salmon running strong, tiger-striped fish crowding into spawning streams, dramatic to watch
42.childFriendlyNote: The rivers are full of big stripy fish! They crowd into shallow water and you can watch them from the bank

42.description: Chanterelle season continuing, golden mushrooms still appearing after every soaking rain
42.childFriendlyNote: After every rainstorm, new golden mushrooms push up through the leaves, nature's treasure hunt keeps going!

42.description: Oyster mushrooms fruiting from dead logs and stumps, shelving clusters of grey-white caps in wet forest
42.childFriendlyNote: Smooth grey shelves of mushroom grow from a dead log like little stairs for fairies. These are oyster mushrooms!

42.description: Varied thrush now common in gardens and lowland woods, foraging in leaf litter and singing in the rain
42.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful orange-breasted bird hops through the wet leaves. Listen for its one long, ringing whistle. Wheeeeeeeee!

42.description: Mosses rapidly re-greening with October rain, bright emerald coating every surface again
42.childFriendlyNote: The whole forest is turning emerald green again! Moss covers everything like a soft fuzzy carpet. Welcome back, rain!

43.description: Chum salmon at peak spawning, pairs on gravel redds, spent fish along the banks feeding the forest
43.childFriendlyNote: Salmon are laying eggs in the gravel. After they lay their eggs, they die and become food for eagles, bears, and even the trees!

43.description: Bald eagles gorging on spawned-out salmon, multiple eagles visible at salmon rivers
43.childFriendlyNote: Eagles swoop down and grab salmon right out of the river! They sit in trees eating fish. You might see ten in one tree!

43.description: Hedgehog mushrooms fruiting in conifer forests, pale orange caps with tiny spines instead of gills underneath
43.childFriendlyNote: Flip over this peachy mushroom and instead of lines underneath, it has tiny spines like a hedgehog! So cool!

43.description: Sword ferns lush again with autumn rain, standing green while deciduous trees lose their leaves
43.childFriendlyNote: While the trees drop their leaves, the sword ferns stay green and tall. They love the rain and never go to sleep for winter!

43.description: Spotted towhees scratching through fallen leaves, making a loud rustling that sounds like a much bigger animal
43.childFriendlyNote: Scratch scratch! A bird with red eyes kicks leaves everywhere. It sounds like a bear is in the bushes but it's just a little towhee!

44.description: Late chum salmon still spawning, many spent fish on banks, the cycle of nutrients returning to the forest
44.childFriendlyNote: The salmon have finished their journey. Their bodies feed the trees, the bugs, and the baby fish that will hatch in spring

44.description: Late-season chanterelles still appearing, along with other autumn fungi in the wet forest
44.childFriendlyNote: Still finding golden mushrooms in the forest! The rain keeps them coming, though the season is winding down

44.description: Oyster mushrooms at peak, beautiful grey-white shelf clusters on dead alder and cottonwood
44.childFriendlyNote: Stacked shelves of smooth grey mushrooms grow right out of a dead tree. They look like a little staircase for mice!

44.description: Varied thrush a constant presence in wet lowland forests and gardens, singing through the rain
44.childFriendlyNote: The varied thrush sings one note that hangs in the misty air. It's the sound of a Pacific Northwest autumn

44.description: Douglas squirrels chattering loudly from conifers, busy cutting and caching Douglas fir cones for winter
44.childFriendlyNote: A tiny rust-coloured squirrel scolds you loudly from a branch. It's guarding its pile of cones like a furry little dragon!

45.description: Mushroom season at peak diversity: chanterelles, hedgehogs, oysters, angel wings, coral fungi all fruiting
45.childFriendlyNote: The forest is a mushroom wonderland! Golden ones, white shelf ones, spiky ones, and ones that look like coral from the ocean!

45.description: Bald eagles still gathering at salmon streams, scavenging spawned-out fish along the banks
45.childFriendlyNote: Eagles line the river like Christmas decorations. Their white heads glow against the dark November sky

45.description: Mosses at full lushness with November rain, every surface coated in vibrant emerald green
45.childFriendlyNote: The whole world is wearing a green velvet coat! Branches, rocks, fences. Moss covers everything and it's so soft

45.description: Large flocks of Oregon juncos at bird feeders and in gardens, a constant winter companion
45.childFriendlyNote: Flocks of cheerful little grey birds hop around the garden. Scatter some seeds and they'll come running!

45.description: Spotted towhees noisily scratching through deep leaf litter, double-footed kicks sending leaves flying
45.childFriendlyNote: The towhee uses both feet at once to kick leaves backwards, scritch, scratch, scritch! Looking for yummy bugs underneath

46.description: Oyster mushrooms still fruiting from dead wood, thriving in cool damp November weather
46.childFriendlyNote: Grey mushroom shelves keep growing from dead logs even in cold November. Fungi don't mind the rain one bit!

46.description: Varied thrush singing its ethereal whistle from every damp forest and backyard, the sound of PNW winter
46.childFriendlyNote: One loooong whistle in the misty garden... then silence... then another note at a different pitch. That's the varied thrush saying hello

46.description: Sword ferns standing green and proud while everything else drops its leaves, anchoring the green winter forest
46.childFriendlyNote: While other plants sleep, the sword ferns keep standing tall and green. They love the cool, rainy winter!

46.description: Bald eagles still abundant near salmon rivers, pairs beginning to reinforce their nest sites for breeding season
46.childFriendlyNote: Eagle pairs are fixing up their huge nests, adding new sticks on top. Some nests are as big as a car!

46.description: Banana slugs active again with autumn rain, bright yellow bodies sliding across wet trails
46.childFriendlyNote: The banana slugs are back! Big yellow slugs slide slowly across the trail leaving shiny silver tracks. They love the rain

47.description: Late mushroom season still going. Look for turkey tail, witch's butter, and hedgehog mushrooms on wet wood
47.childFriendlyNote: Colourful fungi still decorate dead logs: orange jelly blobs (witch's butter!) and stripy turkey tail fans!

47.description: Anna's hummingbirds visiting feeders and late-blooming flowers, the only hummingbird that stays through PNW winter
47.childFriendlyNote: While all other hummingbirds flew south, Anna's hummingbird stays! It's so tough it lives through our rainy winter

47.description: Mosses dripping wet and impossibly green, the forest looks like an enchanted emerald kingdom
47.childFriendlyNote: Everything is so green and so wet! The forest looks like a magical kingdom made of emerald velvet

47.description: Great blue herons standing in winter rain at pond edges, hunched and patient in their grey feather coats
47.childFriendlyNote: The tall grey heron stands in the rain without an umbrella, just waiting and watching, so patient!

47.description: Douglas squirrels still active, eating from their cached cone supplies, chattering from conifer branches
47.childFriendlyNote: The little rust-coloured squirrel is eating the cones it saved! It sits on a branch and shreds them. Cone scales rain down like confetti

48.description: Varied thrush whistling from wet gardens and forests, orange breast visible against grey November landscape
48.childFriendlyNote: An orange-and-black bird glows in the grey garden like a tiny sunset, then sings one beautiful, ghostly note

48.description: Bald eagles perching near water, pairs beginning courtship with spectacular aerial displays
48.childFriendlyNote: Two eagles lock their claws together and tumble through the sky in a spinning cartwheel: that's how they say 'I love you!'

48.description: Licorice ferns green and lush on mossy branches, growing vigorously in the wet winter season
48.childFriendlyNote: Tiny ferns grow right on tree branches in the moss. They come alive in winter when the rain returns!

48.description: Male Anna's hummingbirds singing scratchy songs from exposed perches, defending winter territories
48.childFriendlyNote: Even in cold November, the tiny hummingbird sits on a bare branch and sings a squeaky, buzzy song, so brave!

48.description: Oregon juncos in large winter flocks, trilling and chipping as they forage through leaf litter and under feeders
48.childFriendlyNote: A whole flock of little grey-brown birds hops together under the feeder. They twitter and chip to each other like tiny friends

49.description: Mosses at peak winter lushness, every branch, rock, and fence post wearing a thick green coat
49.childFriendlyNote: The whole forest is wrapped in green velvet! Press your hand on a mossy rock, it's like nature's softest cushion

49.description: Varied thrush singing its single haunting note from dripping December forest, the voice of PNW winter
49.childFriendlyNote: In the misty December woods, one long note rings out and hangs in the air, the most beautiful, ghostly sound

49.description: Turkey tail and other bracket fungi decorating dead logs, jelly fungi wobbling on wet branches
49.childFriendlyNote: Colourful stripy fans grow on dead logs. They're called turkey tail because they look like a turkey spreading its feathers!

49.description: Anna's hummingbirds at feeders in December, puffed up against the cold, magenta gorgets still flashing
49.childFriendlyNote: A tiny puffed-up hummingbird sits on a branch in the rain. It fluffs up its feathers to stay warm like a tiny cotton ball!

49.description: Bald eagles near coastlines and rivers, pairs maintaining nest sites through the winter
49.childFriendlyNote: Even in dark December, the eagle's white head shines in the tall tree. It sits there watching everything!

50.description: Sword ferns evergreen and glistening in winter rain, the backbone of the PNW forest understory
50.childFriendlyNote: Tall green ferns stand in the rain like a forest of feathery swords. They stay green all year long, even in winter!

50.description: Anna's hummingbirds visiting feeders on short December days, needing frequent energy in cold weather
50.childFriendlyNote: The brave little hummingbird visits the feeder dozens of times a day in winter. It needs lots of energy to stay warm!

50.description: Varied thrush foraging on wet ground in gardens and woodland, flipping leaves with its bill
50.childFriendlyNote: The robin-sized bird with the orange breast and black necklace hops in the garden, flipping wet leaves to find tasty worms

50.description: Pacific wrens giving sharp chip notes from tangles of roots and fallen logs in the wet winter forest
50.childFriendlyNote: A mouse-sized brown bird pops out of a log, chips once, and vanishes. The tiny Pacific wren is a master of hide-and-seek!

50.description: Bracket fungi, jelly fungi, and witch's butter decorating dead wood throughout the soggy forest
50.childFriendlyNote: Wobble the orange jelly blob on a branch. It's witch's butter! It bounces back like rubber. Fungi are so weird and wonderful!

51.description: Mosses intensely green in the darkest week of winter, glowing emerald in the forest gloom
51.childFriendlyNote: Even in the darkest, shortest days, the moss glows green like a forest nightlight. Nature never totally goes to sleep here

51.description: Anna's hummingbirds surviving the shortest days, entering torpor at night to save energy, active at feeders by day
51.childFriendlyNote: At night, the hummingbird slows its heart way down to save energy. It almost seems frozen! But come morning, it zooms back to life

51.description: Varied thrush whistling through rain and fog, the defining winter songbird of the Pacific Northwest
51.childFriendlyNote: The misty forest sings one long note... then another... the varied thrush is the voice of our rainy green winter

51.description: Great blue herons standing solitary at winter pond edges, grey plumage blending with grey December skies
51.childFriendlyNote: The tall grey heron is almost invisible against the grey sky and grey water: the best camouflage in winter!

51.description: Licorice ferns green and growing on mossy maple branches, one of the few ferns that grows in winter
51.childFriendlyNote: Ferns grow right on tree branches in winter. This backwards fern sleeps in summer and wakes up in the rain!

52.description: Sword ferns standing green through the darkest days, raindrops dripping from frond tips in the quiet forest
52.childFriendlyNote: Drip... drip... drip... the ferns catch raindrops and let them fall one by one. The winter forest is quiet and green and peaceful

52.description: Varied thrush still singing through the holiday season, one haunting note at a time from the rainy forest
52.childFriendlyNote: On a quiet winter walk, the forest sings you a single beautiful note, happy holidays from the varied thrush!

52.description: Anna's hummingbird at feeders even on the coldest days, the toughest bird in the PNW winter garden
52.childFriendlyNote: Even on the coldest, rainiest day of the year, a jewel-bright hummingbird visits the feeder, the toughest tiny bird around!

52.description: Bald eagles perching near waterways, pairs staying close to nest territories as the year ends
52.childFriendlyNote: As the year ends, the eagle sits in its favourite tree watching the river. It'll be here when the new year begins too

52.description: Banana slugs still active in mild PNW December weather, yellow bodies on the wet forest floor
52.childFriendlyNote: The bright yellow banana slug glides across the wet trail. It doesn't mind winter at all! It leaves a silver path behind like a tiny snail highway
